The function $f(x)$ is defined and differentiable on $[1,6].$ The graph of ${f}^{′}(x),$ the derivative of $f(x),$ is shown above, where the areas of the regions between the graph and the $x$-axis are $2$ and $5,$ respectively (from left to right). Find the maximum value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[1,6]$ given that $f(6)=3.$
question.worked_solution:
According to the candidates test, the maximum value of $f(x)$ on $[1,6]$ must occur at a critical point or an endpoint of the interval.

**Step 1**: Find the critical points:

We see that ${f}^{′}(x)$ is defined everywhere on $x\in (1,6),$ and ${f}^{′}(x)=0$ at $x=2.$ Therefore, the candidates are $x=1,2,6.$

**Step 2**: Compute the value of $f$ for each candidate using the fundamental theorem of calculus:

Using the given information and the fundamental theorem of calculus, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(6) & =3 \\ f(2) & =f(6)+{\int }_{6}^{2}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =f(6)-{\int }_{2}^{6}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3-5 \\  & =-2 \\ f(1) & =f(6)+{\int }_{6}^{1}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =f(6)-{\int }_{1}^{6}{f}^{′}(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3-(5-2) \\  & =3-3 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Select the largest value of $f$ from our candidates.

Comparing the values of $f$ found in step $2,$ we have

$$
{f}_{\text{max}}=max\{3,-2,0\}=3.
$$

Therefore, the maximum value of $f$ is ${f}_{\text{max}}=3,$ and the value of $x$ that maximizes $f(x)$ is ${x}_{\text{max}}=6.$
